questions.question: A destructive tool call needs a human to approve it before the server will run it. How does the server ask for that approval in MCP 2026-07-28?
options: It sends a fresh server-initiated request straight to the client over the still-open connection right away without delay
It returns an input_required result carrying an elicitation/create request, and the client retries with an answer
It refuses the call with a JSON-RPC error until a person runs a separate approval step
It opens a brand new Mcp-Session-Id scoped to this approval and simply waits on that session
questions.explanation: Servers never push requests to the client; a tools/call that needs human approval returns resultType input_required with an elicitation/create inputRequest, and the client answers by retrying with inputResponses and a new id.

questions.question: A client is requesting an access token for an MCP server for the first time, and the 401 challenge carried no scope parameter at all. Which scopes should the client request?
options: A single administrative scope that some human operator chooses on the client's behalf, entirely by hand
No scopes at all, letting the server assign a default working set once the user logs in
Only the scopes the WWW-Authenticate challenge named, or all of scopes_supported if the challenge left that field out
Every scope the authorization server has ever issued to any client, just to save a round trip
questions.explanation: The scope selection strategy is to use the scope from the WWW-Authenticate challenge when one is present, and to fall back to scopes_supported as the minimal starting set when the challenge omits it.

questions.question: A client already holds a token scoped to files:read. A tool call now gets HTTP 403 with error insufficient_scope and scope files:write. What should the client request next?
options: Only files:write, discarding files:read, since the server only asked for the new scope this time only
Every scope the server has ever defined, so no future call can ever trigger a 403 again
Whatever scope the previous tool call in this same session happened to already be using instead
The union of files:read and files:write, so the earlier grant is not lost during re-authorization
questions.explanation: Step-up authorization computes the union of the previously granted scopes and the scopes in the current challenge, so a per-operation scope challenge never silently drops permissions the client already had.

questions.question: A user approves the delete_file tool on a server. What does that one approval cover?
options: Only delete_file itself; a different tool on that same server still needs its own separate approval
Whatever the destructiveHint annotation on the tool currently claims is safe, even once that value changes
Every tool on that server, because the user already trusts the server as a whole from then on
Every future call to delete_file plus any other tool whose name also happens to start with delete
questions.explanation: Consent is scoped to the exact named tool it was granted for, never to a server, a naming pattern, or a category, so a second sensitive tool always needs its own explicit approval.

questions.question: A server's tools/call result comes back with resultType input_required. How must the client's next attempt at that same call be shaped?
options: It must reuse the original request id so the server can match the two attempts to each other, always
It must use a new request id, include inputResponses, and echo requestState back byte for byte as received
It must wait for the server to push a follow-up request instead of retrying on its own
It must open a brand new connection to the server so the retry starts from a clean session
questions.explanation: A multi round-trip retry always carries a new JSON-RPC id, gathers answers into inputResponses under the same keys the server used, and echoes requestState byte for byte if the server sent one.

questions.question: A caller's token carries only payments:read. The server also exposes a send_payment tool gated on payments:write. What should tools/list return to this caller?
options: An error result, because a client should never call tools/list without holding every scope the server defines
The full tool list, but with send_payment marked isError so the model learns not to call it
A tool list that omits send_payment, since the result may vary by the authorization on the request
The full tool list including send_payment, since tools/list must never vary between different callers
questions.explanation: Least privilege applies to list results too: tools/list must not change as a side effect of unrelated requests, but it may vary by the authorization presented, so a caller only sees the tools its current scopes actually permit.
